ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening, at formation and ongoing, of all general partners, limited partners with ≥25% ownership, authorized signatories, beneficiaries of trust/corporate chains and PEPs against: (i) FINTRAC advisories and the PCMLTFA requirements; (ii) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act (including the UN 1267/1373 and 1988 lists); (iii) as commercial best practice for maritime cross-border payments, the OFAC SDN List and FATF 'black/blue' lists. Enhanced due diligence applies to all non-resident PEPs, politically exposed persons and high-risk jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – 'Registre des entreprises' online portal at www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11) and the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises, the name must be in French or include a French version. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated to Latin characters using French standard romanization. A name must be distinctive and not contrary to public order. For a limited partnership, the name must contain 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' (or 'L.P.' in an English version).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a refusal, the applicant may submit a written administrative review request to the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. The Registraire must decide within 30 days. If the refusal is confirmed, the applicant may appeal to the Cour du Québec under the Code of Civil Procedure within 30 days of the final administrative decision, or may re-file a new name reservation with a letter of consent from the conflicting name holder or evidence of acquired distinctiveness. No fee refund is available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as sole registered address for an ISIC 3011 active shipyard; a physical shipyard site and administrative office in Québec are mandatory for provincial licensing (immovable and environmental permits), occupational safety (CNESST) and federal Transport Canada registrations. A virtual office may serve only as an auxiliary mail-forwarding address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, arts. 2236–2262 (société en commandite / limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, arts. 9–54; Regulation respecting fees, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises (Québec Enterprise Registrar), Direction de l'immatriculation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) filed under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None – Quebec law imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow deposit requirement for a registered limited partnership; contributions are fixed entirely by the limited partnership agreement. Foreign partners are permitted provided the general partner is identified in the declaration and, if a legal person, holds the requisite authority or registration to carry on business in Quebec.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED at the first meeting of the General Partner of [●] S.E.C./L.P.: (1) The admission of the limited partners and their agreed capital contributions set out in the limited partnership agreement are ratified; (2) the head office is established at [address], Province of Québec; (3) the General Partner authorizes the filing of the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises and the publication of required statutory notices; (4) [Name] is appointed attorney and authorized signatory for all jurisdictional filings, banking, and tender procedures relating to the shipyard project; (5) the partnership adopts the pro forma constituted documents and shall comply with arts. 2236–2262 of the Civil Code of Québec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise name availability search and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises – online name search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Query the Quebec enterprise name registry to confirm that the proposed limited partnership name is distinctive and not confusingly similar to an existing registered name. If required, submit the fee-bearing name reservation request. Verify that the name includes the compulsory designation 'société en commandite', 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.'
required_dossiers: Name request form (demande de nom d'entreprise)
Identification of the applicant or general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, restyle the name and resubmit a modified declaration within the statutory deadline; if still contested, request administrative review by the director of the Registraire.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of limited partnership agreement and declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Québec notary or licensed legal counsel / governing body of the corporate general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the limited partnership agreement and the signed Declaration of Registration. Record each limited partner's capital contribution, liability limitation, return-of-capital terms, and the unlimited liability of the general partner. If the general partner is a corporation, attach a certified copy of its authorizing board resolution.
required_dossiers: Declaration of registration signed by the general partner
Certified board resolution of the corporate general partner
Foreign registration extract of any non-Quebec partner (extrait de registre), if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any deficiency by re-signature or by a rectifying addendum; obtain a pre-filing opinion from the Registraire's review service where an ambiguity is identified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises – Services en ligne and counter filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed declaration of registration electronically or by mail to the director. Include statutory particulars: enterprise name, head office in Quebec, identity of the general partner and each limited partner, declared contributions, commencement date, and confirmation of an unlimited-liability partner. Pay the statutory fee and preserve the payment receipt.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed by a mandatory
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query or refusal notice is issued, remedy the identified discrepancy and re-file within the prescribed period (generally 30 days); appeal to the Court of Québec if the refusal is maintained.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, GST/QST, payroll and employer account registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (Système d'information de l'inscription et des registres); Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online); Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the attestation of immatriculation, obtain a CRA Business Number through Business Registration Online and activate registrations for GST, Quebec QST, payroll source deductions, and the CNESST employer account. Confirm the head office address and general partner details in all systems.
required_dossiers: Attestation of registration from the Registraire des entreprises
Head office lease or ownership title
General partner identification and incorporation extract
Anticipated payroll and worker classification data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Use the CRA–Revenu Québec cross-registration reconciliation service to eliminate duplicate or mismatched accounts; amend registrations where administrative data discrepancies are detected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) – Shipbuilding and Marine Infrastructure Branch, coordinated with the Québec Ministère de l'Économie, de l'Innovation et de l'Énergie (MEIE)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat d'autorisation pour établissement industriel (Industrial Establishment Certificate of Authorization) under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2, s. 22, complemented by Transport Canada Marine Safety inspection for works affecting navigable waters

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Preliminary environmental evaluation: ocean container vessel shipyards with dry docks, blasting, and coating operations are classified as industrial establishments requiring a full certificate of authorization, an environmental impact notice, and public consultation; a complete project-specific environmental assessment under ÉQA Title II, art. 31 may be triggered if annual steel throughput or dry-dock capacity thresholds are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: prohibition on harmful deposit of oil, sludge, or ship-treating substances into water frequented by fish under Fisheries Act s. 36(3); where a collection and treatment system is installed, final effluent total suspended solids ≤ 30 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 15 mg/L, pH 6.0–9.5. VOCs: marine anti-fouling and topside coatings limited to 500 g/L VOC per CEPA product regulations and the Québec Clean Air Regulation (Q-2, r. 4.1); dry-dock spray booths must use filters achieving ≥ 99% particulate removal efficiency. Waste: sandblasting grit, spent paint, and TBT-containing residues classified as hazardous waste under the Québec Règlement sur les matières dangereuses (Q-2, r. 32) and stored or disposed only under an approved permit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: CNESST workplace health and safety clearance; municipal fire safety inspection certificate under the Fire Safety Act regime; structural load and stability attestation signed by an engineer of the Ordre des ingénieurs du Québec for dry dock walls, slipways, gantry cranes, and emission stacks; municipal industrial occupancy permit; and an approved emergency response plan for hazardous materials storage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) and income tax — digital portal: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses.html); Revenu Quebec for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST), Quebec income tax and employer accounts — digital portal: Revenu Quebec CLIC (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/services-en-ligne/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Register the Quebec limited partnership (societe en commandite) with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) by filing the declaration of registration (Releve d'inscription) and appointing at least one general partner; obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). Step 2 — Apply to the CRA for a federal Business Number (BN) using Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number' or online through CRA 'Register a business'; the partnership is the GST/HST registrant and receives a 15-digit BN (account type RT for GST/HST). Step 3 — Apply to Revenu Quebec for a QST account through CLIC using the BN/NEQ; complete Form LM-1 or the CLIC equivalent for QST registration and, if applicable, Quebec employer payroll deductions. Step 4 — Where partners are non-residents, provide the required declarations (e.g., Form RC151 for non-resident individuals or equivalent corporate attestations) and appoint a Canadian resident agent for service if requested by CRA or Revenu Quebec. Step 5 — File the annual partnership information return (T5013 and Quebec TP-600 equivalent) allocating income/loss to partners; a foreign partner without Canadian registration cannot claim input tax credits on purchases made through the partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — a Quebec limited partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian federal and Quebec income tax purposes: income, losses, and tax credits flow through to the partners, and the partnership itself pays no income tax unless it is a 'specified investment flow-through' for certain investment partnership rules. For GST/HST and QST, however, the partnership is a deemed 'person' and must register separately for the shipyard's commercial activities. No territorial tax-exempt zone applies to the Quebec shipyard; the vessel manufacturing activity is subject to normal Canadian and Quebec tax sovereignty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box classification system; entity classification is determined by the Income Tax Act and provincial partnership law, and a Quebec limited partnership cannot elect to be taxed as a corporation. Hybrid mismatch rules under Income Tax Act sections 18.2 to 18.7 and 20.2 are mandatory and eliminate deduction/non-inclusion mismatches with no elective exception. Available partnership- and indirect-tax elections include: (i) Income Tax Act section 97(4) election to transfer property into the partnership on a tax-deferred rollover basis rather than at fair market value; (ii) Income Tax Act section 249.1 election to adopt a non-calendar fiscal period for the partnership; (iii) Excise Tax Act section 273 'qualifying partnership' election to treat certain supplies between the partnership and its partners as being for fair market value consideration for GST/HST purposes; (iv) Excise Tax Act section 156 election for non-arm's length taxable supplies to be deemed made at fair market value; and (v) for non-resident partners, Income Tax Act section 216 election to pay tax on net Canadian rental income rather than gross withholding. None of these elections alters the pass-through characterization of the limited partnership.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST under the federal Excise Tax Act combined in Quebec with the QST under the Quebec Tax Administration Act — a credit-method value-added consumption tax system (GST at 5% and QST at 9.975% in Quebec; HST at 13–15% applies in participating provinces but not in Quebec).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — a supplier becomes a mandatory GST/HST registrant when worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; the identical CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold applies for QST under the Quebec Tax Administration Act. A Quebec limited partnership shipyard that makes exclusively zero-rated exports may nonetheless voluntarily register for GST/HST and QST to recover input tax credits on shipbuilding inputs; the small-supplier threshold does not apply to non-residents who are not carrying on business in Canada, but the LP shipyard is deemed to be carrying on business in Quebec through its shipyard establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose a real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate. Invoices must contain the prescribed GST/HST/QST information under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec regulations and must be retained by the supplier; e-invoicing is voluntary and aligned with the Pan-Canadian Peppol network. For Quebec public-sector shipbuilding contracts, the supplier must submit electronic invoices through the SEAO (Systeme electronique d'appel d'offres) and meet Quebec public procurement e-invoicing requirements. Export transactions must be reported to the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CAED) or the National Database Management System (NDBMS), and the export records must be reconciled to the zero-rated supply claimed on the GST/HST QST return.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A Quebec shipyard may zero-rate the sale of a newly constructed ocean-going container vessel when the vessel is sold to a non-resident purchaser and is exported from Canada in the course of the sale. The supply qualifies as a zero-rated export of goods under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act, provided the supplier is registered, the vessel is delivered outside Canada, title passes to the non-resident buyer, and the supplier retains satisfactory proof of export. Services performed in respect of the exported vessel (e.g., sea trials, commissioning, and transportation directly related to the export) may also be zero-rated where they are supplied directly in respect of the exported goods. Long-term chartering or leasing of the vessel to a non-resident is not automatically zero-rated unless the vessel is supplied outside Canada and is not made available to the charterer in Canada; the specific charter arrangement must be analyzed separately. The QST zero-rating rules mirror the GST/HST export rules, and the identical documentary evidence must be maintained to support a QST zero-rated supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13 Export Declaration or CAED/NDBMS electronic export filing confirming the vessel's export from Canada
Ocean Bill of Lading (or equivalent contract of carriage) stating delivery at a foreign destination
Signed shipbuilding sale contract and commercial invoice identifying the non-resident purchaser and the Quebec shipyard as seller
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice evidencing the receipt of foreign-currency proceeds in the shipyard's Canadian bank account
Certificate of Vessel Transfer / deletion from the Canadian Registry or flag transfer documentation proving permanent export
Delivery certificate and sea-trial acceptance certificate executed by the purchaser's superintendent at the point of export
Packing list and customs broker's attestation, together with a written GST/HST/QST zero-rating narrative reconciling vessel, components, and services to Schedule VI of the Excise Tax Act
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Quebec audit zero-rated export claims by cross-referencing CBSA export declarations, bank remittance records, contract terms, and corporate registries. If the vessel is not actually exported or the supporting documentation is false or incomplete, the supply is recharacterized as taxable at the Quebec combined rate of 14.975% and the tax is reassessed with compound daily interest under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act and the Quebec Tax Administration Act; the normal four-year reassessment limitation is extended indefinitely where misrepresentation or fraud is established. Specific penalties include: false-statement penalties of CAD 250 to CAD 25,000 under section 285 of the Excise Tax Act; gross-negligence penalties equal to 50% of the federal tax understatement under section 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act; parallel QST penalties and administrative fines up to CAD 25,000 imposed by Revenu Quebec; criminal tax-evasion prosecution under section 286 of the Excise Tax Act with fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment; and clawback of input tax credits previously claimed on shipbuilding inputs, together with interest from the date of the original claim.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating under the Bank of Canada Act, in conjunction with the Department of Finance Canada (Minister of Finance) for statutory currency and exchange-reserve matters, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for prudential supervision of federally chartered banks, FINTRAC for AML/ATF supervision under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA), and the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) as the Quebec provincial regulator for financial product distribution and financial-cooperative oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a free-floating exchange-rate regime with full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII obligations; there is no exchange-control statute (the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951) and no administrative approval is required for foreign investment into a Quebec société en commandite, profit remittances, loan repayments, capital distributions, or liquidation proceeds. The Canadian dollar is fully deliverable, and neither the Bank of Canada nor the Minister of Finance imposes convertibility limits or prioritization of foreign-exchange applications. A Quebec limited partnership engaged in commercial shipbuilding may freely receive capital contributions from non-resident limited partners and remit the pass-through Canadian-source share of profits to those partners, subject only to ordinary Part I income-tax return and installment obligations, treaty-based withholding analysis on payments such as interest or royalties, and mandatory transaction reporting (Statistics Canada balance-of-payments/intra-euro-area reporting, FINTRAC large-value EFT reports, and customs export documentation).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation timeline. A Quebec shipyard that exports deep-sea container vessels, hull blocks, marine components, or engineering services may retain export receipts in any currency in any eligible account at a Canadian Schedule I bank, an authorized foreign bank branch, or a Quebec cooperative credit union (caisse Desjardins). Compliance obligations are limited to: (i) goods-export reporting to Statistics Canada (B13 export declaration for shipments above CAD 2,000); (ii) international services and investment transaction reporting above the applicable Statistics Canada ITRS threshold; and (iii) FINTRAC reporting by the financial intermediary for electronic funds transfers above CAD 10,000. Proceeds may be converted to CAD at will or held in USD/EUR for future procurement of steel plate, marine engines, and outfitting equipment.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational CAD/USD multi-currency account plus segregated Capital Escrow Account for maritime instalment LC drawdowns

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Conditional. Canada does not recognize the European 'Electronic Money Institution' (EMI) licensing category, and a foreign EMI may not take deposits, extend credit, or issue commercial letters of credit in Canada. Digital cross-border payment firms operating in Canada — such as Wise Payments Canada Inc. and Payoneer — must register with FINTRAC as Money Services Businesses (MSBs) under PCMLTFA and may be used only for ancillary, low-value operational outflows (crew payroll, subcontracted engineering fees, small-vendor payments, multi-currency market-rate conversion). They are not viable as primary treasury rails for an ISIC 3011 ocean-container-vessel shipyard because they lack: (i) documented-letter-of-credit issuance and confirmation (UCP 600), (ii) capital-escrow custody and milestone-drawdown certification services, (iii) Lynx/ACSS high-value CAD clearing access, (iv) OSFI-regulated deposit insurance and credit facilities, and (v) sanctions/export-control compliance depth suited to Medium_Risk_Enhanced maritime trade. Feasibility rating: Low for capital injection and LC escrow; Conditional-Medium strictly for non-trade disbursements below CAD 100,000 per transaction.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINTRAC's non-face-to-face identity-verification framework permits account opening using two independent documentary or credit-file verification sources, so remote onboarding is legally possible. In practice, however, banks applying a Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification to a non-resident-investor Quebec limited partnership will mandate: (i) a live video or telephone banker interview with the general partner and a senior officer of the corporate general partner; (ii) notarized or apostilled corporate KYC packs for every non-Canadian partner; (iii) a certified true copy of the attestation d'immatriculation issued by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; and (iv) a signed beneficial-ownership declaration and source-of-funds certificate. For the first capital-escrow drawdown above CAD 5 million, most Big Six banks will additionally require one activation visit by the general partner or its delegated in-house counsel to a commercial banking centre in Montreal, Quebec City, or Trois-Rivières. This physical step is a compliance-policy overlay, not a statutory mandate; it can typically be satisfied through a Quebec-resident attorney-in-fact holding a notarized power of attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque limited-partner ownership: société en commandite whose limited partners include offshore corporate vehicles in Cayman, BVI, or Mauritius
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full upstream ownership chart traced to ultimate natural persons; certified registry extracts for every offshore entity; passport and proof-of-address for each UBO; independent source-of-wealth documentation (private-bank statements, audited financials, tax records); certified copy of the Quebec declaration of registration; executed LP agreement showing capital commitments and a written explanation of the vessel-export commercial rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Atypical high-value maritime payment schedule: front-loaded advance payments or back-to-back instalment LCs from foreign shipowners or charterers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial shipbuilding contract with detailed payment-milestone schedule; classification-society progress certificates (ABS, DNV, Lloyd's Register); escrow instruction letter; pro-forma documentary credit and applicant/beneficiary indemnities; budgeted build-cost forecast aligning inflows to steel, equipment, and labor milestones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions / end-use concern: ocean container-vessel construction triggering controlled-goods, dual-use, or export-control screening of engines, electronics, and emissions equipment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Controlled Goods Program registration certificate issued by ISED; Global Affairs Canada export permit applications and determinations; purchaser end-user/end-use certificate; comprehensive sanctions denial-list screening of shipowner, charterer, and UBOs; internal compliance attestation covering OFAC, UN, EU, and Canadian sanctions regimes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party funding mismatch: incoming wires from family offices, private lenders, or non-bank funds that are not the registered limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed funding or loan agreements; registrations of securities/charges at the Quebec Registraire des entreprises; sworn source-of-funds statements; bank-verified lender identity and wiring instructions; corporate resolution directing that all capital injections be routed only through the LP's single treasury account with exact transaction references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or absent general partner: limited partnership governed by a foreign corporate general partner lacking Canadian nexus
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Appointment of a Quebec-resident attorney or registered agent under the Civil Code of Québec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; certified resolution appointing a Montreal-based compliance officer; irrevocable notarized power of attorney; description of the general partner's unlimited liability and Canadian asset base; declaration of the registered office in Quebec.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Statutory-license discrepancy: shipyard activities requiring federal and provincial permits beyond the business registration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registraire des entreprises business licence and municipal occupational permits; Transport Canada Marine Safety approvals; Environment and Climate Change Canada assessment letters; site lease or ownership evidence; ISED or National Shipbuilding Strategy notifications; certificates from classification societies confirming yard capacity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for non-resident limited-partner capital contributions: (1) All injections must be wired from the partner's own bank account to the LP's designated CAD/USD operational account at the primary Canadian bank; third-party funding is declined unless pre-approved through a formal capital-call resolution and source-of-funds pack. (2) Each MT103 must carry a precise remittance narrative, e.g., 'LP capital contribution per Sec. X of the 2024 Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement — tranche 2 of CAD [amount]'; the bank maps the transaction to the Canada balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment in Canada (equity) or, for passive investors, portfolio-investment equity, rather than to a goods/services code. (3) Settlement occurs through SWIFT, with CAD leg cleared over Lynx and USD leg via the bank's New York correspondent (CHIPS/Fedwire); there is no surrender or conversion mandate, and market-rate conversion is applied if the injection is received in USD. (4) EFTs exceeding CAD 10,000 are automatically reported to FINTRAC; injections exceeding CAD 100,000 are pre-notified to the bank's financial-crime unit with supporting partnership resolutions and beneficial-ownership certificates at least three banking days before value date. (5) The treasury function reconciles each injection against the subscribed capital schedule and records all partner contributions in the LP's capital account ledger to evidence aggregate economic substance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for a commercial container-vessel shipyard: (i) SWIFT MT103 credit transfers for direct cross-border payments to foreign steel mills, marine-engine manufacturers, electrical-systems suppliers, coating vendors, and subcontractors, each supported by purchase orders, invoices, and shipping documents held on file. (ii) Commercial documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 (and URDG 758 for on-demand guarantees/advance-payment bonds) through National Bank / RBC / BMO trade-finance desks, with issuance by MT700, amendments by MT707, negotiation/transfer by MT710/MT720, cover payments by MT202/MT202COV, and confirmation arrangements with Asian and European banks for procurement of engine-room packages and outfitting equipment. (iii) Capital Escrow Account drawdowns: the shipowner or LC-issuing bank deposits each instalment into the segregated escrow; the shipyard draws only upon presentation of a classification-society milestone certificate, a bank-approved drawdown certificate, and corresponding supplier invoices. (iv) Domestic Canadian disbursements (payroll, Quebec subcontractors, Revenu Québec remittances) clear via Lynx for high-value CAD transfers and the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for batched retail items, with overnight sweep into interest-bearing USD/CAD accounts. (v) USD disbursements to U.S. suppliers clear through the Canadian bank's U.S. dollar clearing channel or a U.S. correspondent; every outbound transfer above CAD 10,000 is screened against FINTRAC EFT reporting, OFAC/UN/EU/Canadian sanctioned-party lists, and export-control watchlists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD) executed under a Master Forward Agreement or ISDA 2002 with the primary Canadian bank, requiring collateral under a Credit Support Annex or a working-capital credit facility.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts on non-convertible procurement currencies (offshore CNY/CNH, KRW, INR) for hedging equipment purchases from Asia, available only from credit-approved bank counterparties and booked on an ISDA 1992/2002 master with netting and close-out provisions.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) to convert USD-denominated export-finance or EDC-backed borrowings into CAD floating-rate exposure, and to align interest-payment currency with the LP's operational revenue mix.

FX options and zero-cost collar structures (purchased options, put spreads, call spreads) to protect the USD price of exported vessels and to cap the CAD cost of EUR-denominated European equipment packages.

Rolling spot (tom-next) hedging and FX swaps for short-dated timing gaps between LC cover payments, milestone drawdowns, and supplier settlements, including swap rollovers to prolong hedge tenors without disturbing underlying trade flows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Government of Quebec
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the partnership's registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee CAD 75 (approx. USD 56) if not filed by the deadline; continued non-filing leads to administrative strike-off of the partnership and loss of limited liability protection for limited partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (fiscal year-end income and partner allocations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Federal Government of Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., May 31 for calendar-year fiscal period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per partner per day, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 5,000 per return; stricter penalties for misleading statements.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None under Quebec partnership law; independent audit may be required by the partnership agreement or by bank covenants for shipbuilding financing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS or ASPE as adopted by the partnership; IFRS is typical for shipyard ventures with international lenders.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Limited partnership does not issue capital shares; annual declaration confirms current general partners and any changes in partner composition. No separate annual UBO filing for partnerships is required under Quebec law, but REQ requires disclosure of partners with significant control.
